statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-50651 (GHSA-wp74-jgxh-gv4q) is a .NET denial of service issue in the HTTP client (System.Net.Http): an attacker can use the HTTP/2 protocol to cause an out-of-memory condition. Microsoft lists the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.9 and fixed in 10.0.10 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wp74-jgxh-gv4q, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/422). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release: each build 10.0.N-r0 ships the .NET 10.0.N runtime, and its shared framework reports the dotnet/dotnet source commit it was built from, which for every build from 10.0.3-r0 on is the commit of release tag v10.0.1NN (10.0.9-r0 is v10.0.109, 10.0.10-r0 is v10.0.110 and 10.0.13-r0 is v10.0.113, https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.113) and for 10.0.2-r0 is one commit after tag v10.0.102. Scanned the dotnet10-runtime, dotnet10-runtime-dbg, dotnet10-targeting-pack, dotnet10-apphost-pack, dotnet10-hostfxr, dotnet-host, aspnetcore10-runtime, aspnetcore10-runtime-dbg and aspnetcore10-targeting-pack packages of all 12 published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0, as listed in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository on 2026-11-28) for x86_64 and aarch64, and the dotnet10-runtime-artifacts package of the x86_64 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0 and 10.0.13-r0 builds and the aarch64 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0 builds, including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold. The .NET 10 HTTP client is System.Net.Http.dll in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework in the dotnet10-runtime package; in every scanned build its version is the build's own .NET version, so it is 10.0.2 to 10.0.9 in the first eight builds and 10.0.10 or later from 10.0.10-r0 on, on both architectures. The other copies found are the System.Net.Http reference assembly (metadata only, no code) in dotnet10-targeting-pack and in the Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref nupkg, also at the build's own version, and the .NET Framework System.Net.Http assemblies for net461 and net471 in the SDK's Microsoft.NET.Build.Extensions files (also packed as a nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts), which contain no HTTP/2 client code (no Http2Connection or SocketsHttpHandler type). Of the dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap packages, which hold a .NET SDK, the .NET and ASP.NET Core runtime archives and the runtime packs built from the same source, only the aarch64 10.0.10-r0 package was unpacked. Every implementation copy of System.Net.Http.dll in it (the SDK's shared framework, both runtime archives, and the runtime and NativeAOT runtime packs) is version 10.0.10. The range ends at 10.0.10-r0 because it is the first published build whose HTTP client carries the fix.

Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework, which holds System.Net.Http, at its own .NET version, in dotnet8-runtime and in the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap and in that version's runtime pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap: 8.0.23 to 8.0.27 in the first five builds and 8.0.29 or later from 8.0.29-r0 on. The range ends at 8.0.29-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
